PASS on the fake backend (G1-G9, no warning). Re-authored by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human; run p3-reauthor-qcdrivers, 2026-11-05) under the user's decision of 2026-11-05 (Claude authors, Claude Sonnet reviews). It replaces the DeepSeek package (deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run helper-wave-1-013), blocked on G8 TCAP-003 after review; that package, its RESULT.json and its review paragraphs are kept in work/handoff-runs/claude-20261104/development/p3-reauthor/moved-aside/labs/squad-lab__qcdrivers/. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper is PythonObjectDriver over the override entry qcdrivers.squad.mux.mux:Muxi; this is a decorated direct Driver over the same class, because a Python-object result map cannot report the route sent and the firmware prints more lines than the class's methods read. WHAT IT DOES: every command goes out with the upstream handle's query (the call send_command makes, mux.py:86) and further lines are read with the handle's read (as printconfig does, mux.py:171), one exchange at a time under a lock (a connect holds it across SWITCH32 and its read-back); send_command, switch32 and reset are not called (their retry path raises AttributeError on a VISA timeout, mux.py:87-90, and reset reads one of the two *RST lines). connect sends SWITCH32 x,y, requires the firmware's 'Route added 32x32' (firmware.ino:84) and reads the route back with STAT? x,y (two labelled lines, firmware.ino:90-106); it reports x, y, the reply and the 32x32 route-buffer bit. status reads that bit (R0). reset_matrix and the e-stop send *RST and accept only this command's own 'Clear complete' then 'Reset complete' (firmware.ino:111, then firmware.ino:55), read after every line still owed by an earlier command: one for *IDN? (firmware.ino:48), one for SWITCH32 (firmware.ino:78 or 84), two for STAT? (firmware.ino:98-102) and two for an earlier *RST. loop processes one command at a time (firmware.ino:43-44), so those owed lines are printed before this pair. connect and reset_matrix check for cancellation under the line lock right before they write (the server cancels operations before it stops), so neither writes after the e-stop's *RST. The e-stop declares latency_ms 5000: it may wait for one connect in progress, whose reads are each bounded by the 2000 ms VISA timeout (mux.py:55) and end the exchange when one times out; a slower line fails the first e-stop receipt (latch kept, retried). The identity read sends *IDN? and accepts only the firmware's 'SQUAD,' line. A pin the firmware refuses (12-15, 28-31) fails PRECONDITION_UNMET; a transport error after an effectful command, or an unexpected reply line, is an unknown outcome. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: STAT? and 'Reset complete' report the firmware's route buffers and its completion of the shift-out, not the analog switches (isRouted reads the buffer, AD75019_24.cpp:91-93; nothing senses the chips). The 16x16 line of STAT? is checked for its label only: for a pin above 15 the firmware reads past the 16-entry mappings (firmware.ino:95, AD75019.cpp:79-82, AD75019.h:124-125). Not covered: SWITCH16, CLEAR, PRINT, full_status (a placeholder matrix) and the repository's other instruments (add_parameter QCoDeS drivers). LIMITS: the X and Y pins of connect and status are operator_required (the cabled pin set is deployment data); site-limits.example.json narrows an example bench to pins 0-11. FAKE: fake.py emulates the clone's firmware sketch line by line (its literal reply strings, its route buffers, unread lines kept in order); the 16x16 bit above pin 15 is a placeholder. HARDWARE: native.connect builds the upstream Muxi (pyVISA session, connect_message to stdout, buffer clear; it does not reset the switch). R1. PUBLICATION: the card says publish_review required (AGPL-3.0): the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before the owner decides. FOR THE HUMAN REVIEWER: confirm the firmware actually flashed on the switch is this firmware.ino. BL-19, repaired 2026-11-05: a reset *RST whose reads timed out, then a SWITCH32 whose read also timed out, leaves that *RST's 'Clear complete' and 'Reset complete' and the route line unread, and the route stays closed. The e-stop reads those owed lines and confirms only when the next two are this [...]

MODEL REVIEW (grok-4.7, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): BL-19 repair, round 2. The e-stop confirms only on the two lines after the owed prefix. An ordinary exchange yields while that prefix is unread, and again after the last owed line, before this command's own reply, when len(taken) <= prefix (driver.py:226). Connect checks cancellation and estop_epoch before STAT? (driver.py:346-348). A state read has no cancel context; _engage_estop advances the epoch before stop waits for the line lock. The e-stop's own *RST is not preemptable, so the first query transmits it once the line is free. With one owed *IDN? line and each later read at 1.6 s, client.estop sends *RST at 1.605 s, the route is clear and the receipt is completed. A copy that yields only while len(taken) < prefix sends it at 3.210 s. The forty-line drain and the stale-pair tests still pass. A served reset plus connect owes seven lines: four *IDN? reads, the *RST pair and SWITCH32. The served failure case uses driver.estop because a failed client.estop retries after 0.25 s (server.py:176). 27 package tests passed in 8.814 s, including the gate. Gate digest sha256:8d2080129ff09ec438d5e2e3feb09574afccb9df6cc1a2ca4ba0c830e19f8b87, unchanged. Evidence is contract_checked on the fake only.
